mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, higher interest rates may reduce borrowing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 5% but S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low UNRATE and rising PAYEMS indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Low UNRATE and high PAYEMS but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising INDPRO during economic expansion signals increased productivity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing HOUST indicates housing market strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% may indicate economic overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 3.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS increases and FEDFUNDS decreases, it signals strong consumer demand and easing monetary policy, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth and FEDFUNDS decline but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS leads to decreased investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
